# App-kit assessment — 2026-09-13

App-kit already delivers shared tokens, charts, components, a Gallery, and CLI
primitives. The main opportunity is to make complete, excellent user experiences
repeatable and to prove that improvements reach consumers. More component inventory
or another MCP server alone will not establish that outcome.

## Evidence boundary

This is a source audit of app-kit and a representative consumer sample:
Throughline, resume_as_code (RAC), Growing Gardens BI, Car Assistant, ESP Thumper,
and selected Bosun integration. It is not a full fleet audit. Browser observations
cover the local Gallery only; downstream apps were not visually inspected.
Source presence proves implementation or integration, not runtime correctness,
accessibility conformance, or user satisfaction. Tests cited below were inspected;
their presence is not a claim that the consumer suites were run for this assessment.

Current implementation is separated below from the newly accepted direction in
[scope](../intent/scope.md), [experience system](../design/experience-system.md),
and [adoption](../design/adoption.md). Those documents own goals and work sequencing;
this dated assessment owns the observations, not another backlog.

## Ranked findings

### 1. The last mile of shared behavior still lives independently in apps

Car Assistant explicitly says the kit's mobile Menu is easy to miss and adds its
own persistent bottom navigation ([render.go, line 68](../../../car-assistant/internal/web/render.go#L68),
[implementation, line 98](../../../car-assistant/internal/web/render.go#L98)). This
is concrete consumer feedback for navigation design, not an inferred visual defect.

Its [theme toggle, line 156](../../../car-assistant/internal/web/render.go#L156)
and [Growing Gardens' toggle, line 199](../../../growing-gardens-bi/internal/web/render.go#L199)
have identical markup. Both independently build document/theme bootstraps and
authenticated actions around `dashboard.RenderShell`
([Car Assistant, line 55](../../../car-assistant/internal/web/render.go#L55),
[Growing Gardens, line 30](../../../growing-gardens-bi/internal/web/render.go#L30)).
RAC's independent [navigation, line 39](../../../resume_as_code/cmd/serve/shell.go#L39)
adds `aria-current="page"`, while Car Assistant's sidebar links do not.

Implication: shared shell, navigation, appearance, and account recipes can spread
behavioral improvements. Product destinations, permissions, and business rules
must remain consumer-owned.

### 2. Analytics correctness needs reusable contracts, not just chart functions

RAC's [chart lint, lines 3–23](../../../resume_as_code/tests/lint/charts_test.go#L3)
records defects that escaped while using kit charts: multiple color roles without
a legend and a sparkline displaying only its peak. It now inspects AST call sites
for legends, printed bar values, and last-value annotations. The
[real scan, line 370](../../../resume_as_code/tests/lint/charts_test.go#L370) and
[coverage canary, line 384](../../../resume_as_code/tests/lint/charts_test.go#L384)
are useful upstream candidates, subject to generalizing their assumptions.

Growing Gardens demonstrates the higher-value workflow: period-sensitive metrics
and interpretation around kit widgets
([cost dashboard, lines 16–95](../../../growing-gardens-bi/internal/web/handlers_dashboards.go#L16)).
The kit should supply presentation contracts for units, periods, comparisons,
unknowns, freshness, sources, and drill-down; the consumer supplies financial formulas
and domain-specific judgments.

### 3. Agent instructions vary by harness and consumer

Throughline's [CLAUDE.md, lines 100–110](../../../throughline/CLAUDE.md#L100)
requires kit discovery, token adaptation, upstreaming, and browser verification.
Its [AGENTS.md](../../../throughline/AGENTS.md) contains only the fathom stanza.
Car Assistant similarly has [kit rules in CLAUDE.md, line 50](../../../car-assistant/CLAUDE.md#L50)
but only fathom guidance in [AGENTS.md](../../../car-assistant/AGENTS.md).
Growing Gardens' [CLAUDE.md](../../../growing-gardens-bi/CLAUDE.md) and
[AGENTS.md](../../../growing-gardens-bi/AGENTS.md) both contain only fathom guidance.

No root `.mcp.json` was present in these five sampled app repos; global registration
can supply MCP access, so this does not prove that their MCPs are unavailable.
The adopted direction is one short maintained routing contract installed in both
harnesses, with consumer constraints and verification evidence made explicit.

### 4. Distribution does not yet make propagation effortless

Local sibling `replace` directives remain in
[Throughline go.mod, line 33](../../../throughline/go.mod#L33),
[RAC, line 78](../../../resume_as_code/go.mod#L78),
[Growing Gardens, line 51](../../../growing-gardens-bi/go.mod#L51), and
[Car Assistant, line 53](../../../car-assistant/go.mod#L53).
The local app-kit tag list was empty when inspected.

RAC still imports the sibling theme from four levels up
([input.css, line 11](../../../resume_as_code/cmd/serve/web/input.css#L11)). Its
[CSS script, lines 7–28](../../../resume_as_code/cmd/serve/web/build-css.sh#L7)
hardcodes a macOS ARM cache location and checks for that sibling theme. Existing
[multi-target plan, lines 240–248](../plans/multi-target-kit.md#L240) defers the
release and consumer migration. Kit-side machinery is not proof of consumer uptake.

### 5. Layered adoption works; its provenance needs a more honest receipt

ESP Thumper intentionally adopts the token vocabulary and declines Go UI packages
to preserve a documented main-binary dependency constraint
([theme.css, lines 4–17](../../../esp-thumper/internal/adapter/web/shared/assets/theme.css#L4),
[ADR-0029, lines 82–94](../../../esp-thumper/docs/adr/0029-agentic-kit-only.md#L82)).
That is a supported adoption shape, not a reason to force more imports.

Its [Taskfile, lines 67–68](../../../esp-thumper/Taskfile.yml#L67) skips vendor
verification if `web/vendor/appkit/kit.lock` is absent; that file and `web/input.css`
were absent, while [web tasks](../../../esp-thumper/taskfiles/web.yml) still reference
those paths. Current CSS lives under `internal/adapter/web/`. Vocabulary adoption
and verified generated-artifact provenance must be reported separately.

Its isolated [thumperctl TUI, lines 11–28](../../../esp-thumper/cmd/thumperctl/strip_tui.go#L11)
does consume cli-kit and Bubble Tea. Bosun uses shared diagnostic output
([doctor.go, lines 14–24](../../../platform-engineering/kits/env-kit/internal/cmd/doctor.go#L14)).
CLI-kit is already a real subkit with consumers, not a proposal to start from zero.

## MCP and Gallery baseline

The MCP registers **10 tools** in [tools.go](../../cmd/appkit-mcp/tools.go).
Component search/fetch defaults to TailwindPlus and alternatively accepts MatDash
([source schema, line 23](../../cmd/appkit-mcp/tools.go#L23)); native kit components
are not a searchable source. There is no shared capability registry connecting
native offerings, specimens, maturity, adoption requirements, and consumer evidence.
Startup requires the TailwindPlus SQLite index before loading kit guidance
([main.go, lines 66–86](../../cmd/appkit-mcp/main.go#L66)), so a missing licensed
corpus also prevents otherwise independent guidance tools from starting.

Compatibility metadata is already misleading: the local
[MatDash manifest, line 97](../../data/matdash/packages/main/package.json#L97)
declares Tailwind `^3.4.16`, but [the importer, lines 145–199](../../internal/matdash/walk.go#L145)
preserves raw source and hardcodes Tailwind version `4`. All **762** local indexed
records report `4/react/none`; that label is not proof of a Tailwind 4 conversion.
The [dashboard design, line 59](../design/dashboards-and-matdash.md#L59) also says
MatDash has no real charting, despite its manifest declaring
[`apexcharts` 3.48.0](../../data/matdash/packages/main/package.json#L31) and
[`react-apexcharts` ^1.4.1](../../data/matdash/packages/main/package.json#L51).
Correcting source-versus-adapted compatibility claims is an immediate G1 input.

The Gallery exists and launches locally. It has **11 manually registered page
routes** ([gallery.go, lines 33–43](../../apps/gallery/gallery.go#L33)); it is not a
registry-generated catalog. Its overview still describes a tokens-plus-viz baseline,
despite the broader navigation. The dashboard specimen contains five `href="#"`
navigation links and an unwired New case button
([render.go, lines 742–753](../../apps/gallery/render.go#L742)).

Browser inspection on 2026-09-13 used Chrome at
`http://127.0.0.1:18765/dashboard`: viewport width **1300 CSS px**, document
`scrollWidth` **1378 px**; horizontal overflow was observed. The rendered page had
**two nested `main` landmarks**, five visible placeholder navigation links, and
clicking New case produced no workflow. These findings concern this Gallery
composition; they do not establish equivalent failures in downstream apps.

The accepted direction is to evolve this Gallery into a living experience workbench
and share its capability metadata with the existing MCP. Registry, complete recipes,
consumer receipts, and automated checks described in the design are not yet shipped.

## External technology snapshot

On 2026-09-13, [Wails v3 status](https://v3.wails.io/status/) describes beta desktop
support with mobile experimental. Desktop support must be verified per target;
iOS/Android are future options, not a present kit compatibility promise.

Current [Datastar security guidance](https://data-star.dev/reference/security)
documents nonce-based CSP support. Its applicability must be tested against the
kit's pinned release and expression usage before revisiting accepted security
constraints. Newer upstream documentation does not authorize silently changing the
kit's CSP policy.

## What would demonstrate improvement

A consumer declares its layers, runtime, constraints, kit revision, and divergences;
one representative workflow has dated behavior/browser evidence, meaningful states,
and a reproducible asset build. A repeated pattern or escaped defect then produces a
kit improvement or documented exception, a specimen/check, and verified downstream
adoption. Measure task usefulness, similar-screen delivery effort, defects prevented,
update lag, and improvements reaching another app. Component-import counts and the
number of available MCP tools cannot substitute for these outcomes.
